sections.h2: Which sale routes suit an Austin owner who needs to move quickly?
sections.html:
Austin owners generally choose between a standard listing, a self-managed sale and a straight cash purchase. A cash buyer closes on a date you pick and accepts the house as it stands, whereas a listing depends on showings, appraisals and the next buyer's financing.

Prices run high. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures put a typical owned home at $555,300, and only 43.4 percent of households own the home they occupy. With so many renters, plenty of Austin houses have been rentals or could become one, which affects what an investor will pay and how fast the deal can move.

  • Standard listing: fits an updated house priced near its closest comparable sales, with weeks to spare for showings and a buyer's lender.
  • Self-managed sale: you handle pricing, contracts and negotiation, and a title company still runs the closing.
  • Cash purchase: fits deferred maintenance, an inherited house, a tenant in place or a hard deadline.

sections.h2: How did Austin become the city it is, and what does that mean for homes here?
sections.html:
Austin was laid out in 1839 as the capital of the Republic of Texas, and its housing reflects waves of growth from the capital's early grid to the high-tech boom of the late twentieth century. Commissioners bought 7,735 acres along the Colorado River that included the hamlet of Waterloo, then platted a 640-acre grid between Waller Creek on the east and Shoal Creek on the west, split by Congress Avenue.

The city won the statewide vote to stay the capital in 1872, and the University of Texas was chosen as its site in 1881. Dams on the Colorado River in 1940 and 1941 ended the flooding that had ravaged the town and created Lake Austin and Lake Travis. High technology took off after IBM located here in 1967, followed by Texas Instruments in 1969 and Motorola in 1974.

Rapid growth drew pushback as early as the 1970s. Neighborhood groups organized against dense apartment building and traffic, and environmental ordinances protected creeks, lakes and wooded hills. Those rules still shape what owners can build or change, so a seller with an unpermitted addition or a lot near a creek should expect the buyer's inspector and the title company to ask questions.

sections.h2: How large and how costly is the Austin housing market?
sections.html:
Austin's July 2025 population estimate is 1,002,632, about 4.6 percent above the April 2020 estimates base of 958,151. The 2010 Census counted 790,390.

sections.h2: Does Austin regulate short-term rentals, and does it matter if I sell?
sections.html:
Yes. Austin licenses short-term rentals, and the license cannot be transferred, so a buyer who wants to keep renting by the night has to apply for a new one.

In February 2025 the City Council made short-term rental an accessory use to residential uses in all zoning districts, as long as the operator holds a valid license. Changes that took effect in October 2025 lengthened licenses to two years and dropped the certificate of occupancy and insurance proof for new applicants and renewals. Tenants can now operate a short-term rental with the landlord's permission.

  • On a single-family site, one person may run up to two units, and any further rentals must sit at least 1,000 feet apart.
  • On multifamily sites the limit is the greater of one unit or 10 percent of the units.
  • The local contact must be in Travis, Williamson, Hays, Bastrop or Caldwell County and able to respond within two hours.
  • Neighbors within 100 feet receive notice of the local contact at each issuance and renewal.
  • Booking platforms must display license numbers and take down unlicensed listings when the city asks, under rules that began July 1, 2026.

Properties in the extraterritorial jurisdiction do not need a city license or local hotel tax registration, so the jurisdiction map matters. The city's short-term rental page explains how to check where a parcel falls.

sections.h2: How do homestead exemptions and the appraisal cap affect an Austin sale?
sections.html:
If you live in the house, your taxable value is probably below the market value a buyer sees on the listing. Texas school districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead, and the appraised value of a homestead cannot rise more than 10 percent a year beyond new improvements.

That cap follows the owner who claimed the exemption, so an investor starts without it. Ask the title company to show the first full year's tax for the buyer so the contract holds no surprise. Homeowners 65 or older, or disabled, also receive $60,000 more in school exemption and a school tax ceiling that can transfer to a new Texas homestead.

Travis County's tax office explains that the Travis Central Appraisal District grants exemptions while the tax office collects bills; its tax breaks page links to each one. The Comptroller's limitations page covers the cap and the ceiling.

sections.h2: What steps and paperwork close an Austin sale?
sections.html:
The deed is the closing document. It must be acknowledged before a notary, or sworn before two witnesses, before the county clerk will record it.

  1. Collect your deed, payoff letters and the latest tax statement.
  2. Request a payoff for any lien, since each year's tax lien attaches January 1.
  3. Check which county records the deed for your parcel, because the city is large.
  4. Sign the settlement papers and deed, and let the title company file the deed.

An inherited house adds a title question: an executor's deed, a muniment of title order or an affidavit of heirship. The last is a sworn statement that no law makes a third party accept, so ask early which one the title insurer will honor.

sections.h2: How should I compare offers on an Austin house?
sections.html:
Compare what lands in your account and when, not the headline figure. A higher price loaded with repair credits, a long financing window and a commission can net less than a lower cash bid with a firm date.

Ask each buyer how they treat tenants, unpermitted work and open code complaints, and whether the bid survives an inspection. Note each deadline in writing and choose the offer that clears your payoff and fits your move.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental license transfer to the buyer of my Austin house?
faqs.a: No. The city says operating licenses cannot be transferred, so a buyer must apply for a new one. Give the buyer your license history so the application goes smoothly.
Austin is the Travis County seat, and the city sits in the central part of the county. Check your tax bill for the county of record on your parcel, since it decides which clerk files the deed.

faqs.q: Do I lose my homestead cap when I sell my Austin house?
faqs.a: Your own exemption ends when you stop living there. The 10 percent cap starts on January 1 of the year after an owner first qualifies for the homestead exemption, so a buyer who moves in and claims it begins a new cap period, while a buyer who rents the house out does not.

faqs.q: What if my Austin house has unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: The balance is paid out of your sale proceeds, because the lien sticks to the property. Unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

faqs.q: What is Austin's population and size?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 1,002,632 residents for 2025, a 4.6 percent rise over the 2020 base. The land area is 319.94 square miles.
